Prealgebra · Lesson 7.4

Proportions

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Writing ab=cdba​=dc​ is a proportion. Two quantities are proportional when their ratio stays constant. The coming shortcut, cross-multiplication, is just clearing denominators from Chapter 6.

Problem
A fountain pours at 9 liters per minute. You timed it for 2 minutes and caught 18 liters, and a friend measured 45 liters in 5 minutes. Keeping that same flow, how many liters pour out in 8 minutes?
Show a hint
  • Because the flow is proportional, the ratio of minutes to liters stays the same at every moment. Write two equal ratios with minutes on top and liters on the bottom in both, using xx for the unknown liters. One side is the 22 minute reading, the other is the 88 minute pour. That gives you 218=8x182​=x8​.
  • To solve a proportion, cross-multiply. For ab=cdba​=dc​ the cross products are equal, so a⋅d=b⋅ca⋅d=b⋅c. Apply that to 218=8x182​=x8​ to clear the denominators, then solve the simple equation for xx.
Show the full solution
Keep minutes on top and liters on the bottom on both sides. 218=8x182​=x8​ Cross-multiply, so 2x=18⋅8=1442x=18⋅8=144, and dividing by 22 gives 7272​ liters. Quick sanity check, the flow is 99 liters per minute and 9×8=729×8=72.
Problem
A camp kitchen uses 2 cups of rice for every 5 campers. Tonight 15 campers arrive. How many cups of dry rice are needed?
Show a hint
  • Set two equal ratios side by side, keeping cups on top and campers on the bottom in both. That gives 25=x1552​=15x​, where xx is the cups you want. Now look at the camper side. What did 55 get multiplied by to become 1515?
  • Notice that 5×3=155×3=15, so the campers grew by a factor of 33. To keep the ratio equal, the cups have to grow by that same 33. If scaling feels shaky, cross-multiply instead, which turns 25=x1552​=15x​ into 5x=2×155x=2×15.
Show the full solution
Cups on top, campers on the bottom on both sides. 25=x1552​=15x​ The campers went from 55 to 1515, a jump of ×3×3, so the cups take the same ×3×3, giving 2×3=62×3=6​ cups. Cross-multiplying gets there too, since 5x=2×15=305x=2×15=30. Scaling is just faster when the multiplier is a clean whole number.
Key idea
Two quantities are proportional when their ratio stays the same at every scale, 99 liters per minute whether you wait 22 minutes or 5050. Setting one such ratio equal to another, like 91=x819​=8x​, gives a proportion, an equation that says two ratios match. That is the equivalent-ratio idea from 7.1 as an equation. To solve one by scaling, find the number that multiplies the known side to the new side, then multiply the other term by that same number to get the unknown. Scaling is quick when that multiplier is a simple double or triple, and slow when it is not a whole number.
Problem
A paint mix calls for 8 jars of pigment in 14 liters of base. A big order needs 20 jars. Set up 814=20x148​=x20​ and solve. How many liters of base are needed?
Show a hint
  • Write a proportion with the same units in the same spots on both sides. Keep jars on top and liters on the bottom, so 8 jars14 liters=20 jarsx liters14 liters8 jars​=x liters20 jars​.
  • You can clear both denominators at once. Multiply each numerator by the other side's denominator, which gives 8⋅x=14⋅208⋅x=14⋅20, then solve the equation 8x=2808x=280.
Show the full solution
Jars on top, liters on the bottom in both ratios. 814=20x148​=x20​ Multiply both sides by 1414 and by xx. The 1414 cancels on the left and the xx cancels on the right, leaving 8x=14⋅20=2808x=14⋅20=280, so x=2808=35x=8280​=35​ liters. That step, each numerator times the other side's denominator, is what cross-multiplication is. It is the fraction-clearing move from 6.2 done to both denominators at once.
Problem
A 3D printer uses 5 grams of filament for 8 layers. How many grams does a 6-layer piece need? (There is no clean whole-number scale from 8 to 6, so use cross-multiplication.)
Show a hint
  • Both ratios compare the same two things, grams and layers, so keep grams on top and layers on the bottom in both fractions. The test gives 5885​, and the unknown grams over the 66 layers gives x66x​. Set them equal as 58=x685​=6x​.
  • You cannot scale 88 to 66 cleanly, so cross-multiply instead. Multiply each numerator by the other denominator to clear the fractions, which turns 58=x685​=6x​ into 8x=5×68x=5×6. Then divide both sides by 88.
Show the full solution
Grams on top, layers on the bottom on both sides. 58=x685​=6x​ Cross-multiply to get 8x=5×6=308x=5×6=30, then divide by 88, so x=308=15/4x=830​=15/4​ grams, which is 3.753.75. No whole-number multiplier carries 88 to 66, so scaling has nothing to grab, but cross-multiplication never needs one.
Problem
A map uses the scale 6 cm = 10 km. Two overlooks are 9 km apart on the trail. How many centimeters apart are they on the map?
Show a hint
  • Write two ratios that must be equal, with real kilometers on top and map centimeters on the bottom in both. The first pair gives 106610​, and the second pair gives 9xx9​, so your proportion is 106=9x610​=x9​ with the unknown sitting in a denominator.
  • Cross-multiply just like always, top times opposite bottom equals top times opposite bottom, which gives 10x=6×910x=6×9. A denominator unknown is no harder, since cross-multiplication treats both slots the same way. Work out the right side, then divide both sides by 1010 to free xx.
Show the full solution
Real kilometers on top, map centimeters on the bottom in both ratios. 106=9x610​=x9​ Cross-multiply to get 10x=6×9=5410x=6×9=54, so x=5410=27/5x=1054​=27/5​ centimeters, which is 5.45.4. The unknown sat in a denominator this time, and cross-multiplication treated it exactly like a numerator.
Key idea
Cross-multiplication. When two ratios are set equal, ab=cdba​=dc​, multiply each numerator by the opposite denominator to get ad=bcad=bc, which has no fractions. It works because cross-multiplying is multiplying both sides by both denominators at once, so they cancel and the equation stays true. It is the same clearing step from 6.2. Scaling is faster when the multiplier is an easy whole number, but cross-multiplication needs no such multiplier, so it solves every proportion, even when the answer is a fraction or a decimal.
Problem
A harbor kiosk trades at one fixed rate: 7 dollars gets 91 shells. How many shells does the traveler get for 11 dollars?
Show a hint
  • The rate is the same both times, so the ratio of dollars to shells is constant. Write one proportion with dollars on top and shells on the bottom in both fractions, 791=11x917​=x11​, so the matching units line up.
  • Now cross-multiply. Multiply 77 by xx and set it equal to 91×1191×11, then divide to get xx by itself.
Show the full solution
Dollars on top, shells on the bottom in both ratios. 791=11x917​=x11​ Cross-multiply to get 7x=91⋅11=10017x=91⋅11=1001, so x=10017=143x=71001​=143​ shells. The rate confirms it, since 791=113917​=131​ and 11143=11314311​=131​, thirteen shells per dollar both times.
Problem
A 3-inch mast represents 90 real inches. The boom is 5 inches. A student writes 390=x5903​=5x​ with mixed units. Set it up correctly. What is the real boom length in inches?
Show a hint
  • Keep matching units in matching positions so each side reads the same rate. Put real inches on top and model inches on the bottom for both ratios. The mast gives 903390​, and the boom gives x55x​, so write 903=x5390​=5x​.
  • Clear the fractions by cross-multiplying. From 903=x5390​=5x​ you get 3x=90×53x=90×5. Work out the right side, then divide both sides by 33 to find xx.
Show the full solution
Put real inches on top and model inches on the bottom on both sides. 903=x5390​=5x​ Cross-multiply to get 3x=90×5=4503x=90×5=450, so x=4503=150x=3450​=150​ inches. The student's setup had model over real on one side and real over model on the other, which sets two different rates equal and gives a wrong answer.
Key idea
Match units before cross-multiplying. A proportion only works when matching units sit in matching positions, so the tops of both sides measure the same kind of thing, and so do the bottoms. Then each side is the same rate, such as real over model on both sides, or miles over inches on both sides. If you flip one side by accident, cross-multiplication still produces a number, but it multiplies the wrong quantities, so that number is wrong. Read both sides aloud first to check that the units match.
Problem
A trail-snack recipe uses 5 scoops oats for every 2 scoops cashews. A big batch needs 12 scoops of oats. How many scoops of cashews keep the ratio right?
Show a hint
  • Write the proportion with matching units in matching spots. Put oats on top and cashews on the bottom on both sides, 52=12x25​=x12​. The recipe ratio sits on the left, and the big batch sits on the right with the unknown cashews as xx.
  • Jumping from 55 oats to 1212 oats is not a clean whole-number scale, so cross-multiply instead of guessing. Multiply each top by the opposite bottom to get 5⋅x=2⋅125⋅x=2⋅12, then solve for xx.
Show the full solution
Oats on top, cashews on the bottom on both sides. 52=12x25​=x12​ Cross-multiply to get 5x=2⋅12=245x=2⋅12=24, so x=24/5x=24/5​ scoops, which is 4.84.8. Going from 55 oats to 1212 is not a whole-number jump, so scaling is no help and cross-multiplication does the work.
Problem
A park ranger measures a 6-foot rod casting an 8-foot shadow. Across the field, a fire-watch antenna casts a 28-foot shadow at the same instant. How tall is the antenna in feet?
Show a hint
  • The rod and the antenna make the same shape, so height over shadow is the same for both. Write one ratio for the rod and set it equal to the same kind of ratio for the antenna, keeping height on top and shadow on the bottom in both. That gives 68=h2886​=28h​.
  • Now clear the fractions by cross-multiplying. Multiply the 66 by the 2828 and set it equal to 88 times hh, then divide both sides to get hh by itself.
Show the full solution
Height over shadow is the same for both, since the sun hits the rod and the antenna at the same slant. 68=h2886​=28h​ Cross-multiply to get 8h=6⋅28=1688h=6⋅28=168, so h=1688=21h=8168​=21​ feet. A rod you can reach gives you the ratio, and that ratio measures anything else standing in the same sunlight.
Fun fact
Thales reportedly found a pyramid's height by measuring its shadow when the sun made height equal shadow. Parallel sun rays create similar triangles, the proportion method in this lesson.
Problem
At a craft fair, 6 bundles cost 15 dollars at a fixed price. You want 10 bundles. How many dollars do 10 bundles cost?
Show a hint
  • Two ratios that match describe the same fixed price, so set them equal. Keep the units lined up, bundles over dollars on each side, with the unknown cost as xx, which gives 615=10x156​=x10​.
  • Clear the fractions by cross-multiplying. Multiply each numerator by the other side's denominator, so 6⋅x=15⋅106⋅x=15⋅10, then divide to get xx by itself.
Show the full solution
Bundles on top, dollars on the bottom in both ratios. 615=10x156​=x10​ Cross-multiply to get 6x=15⋅10=1506x=15⋅10=150, so x=1506=25x=6150​=25​ dollars. The unit rate from 7.3 lands in the same place, since one bundle is 15÷6=2.515÷6=2.5 dollars and 2.5×10=252.5×10=25.
Key idea
Two ways to solve a proportion. A proportion says that two rates are equal, and cross-multiplying is not the only way to solve one. You can instead find the unit rate from 7.3, which is the value for one, then multiply it by the amount you need. Both methods give the same answer. Cross-multiplication always works, and the unit-rate method is faster when one side divides evenly.
Problem
A mural is 5 ft tall and 12 ft wide. A scaled-up copy is 20 ft tall. How many feet wide is the big copy?
Show a hint
  • Keep matching positions in matching positions. Put the two heights together and the two widths together, so the small mural's height over its width equals the big copy's height over its width. With xx as the unknown width, that is 512=20x125​=x20​.
  • Now clear the fractions by cross-multiplying. The product across one diagonal equals the product across the other, so 5⋅x=12⋅205⋅x=12⋅20. Work out the right side, then divide both sides by 55 to get xx.
Show the full solution
Small height over small width equals big height over big width. 512=20x125​=x20​ Cross-multiply to get 5x=12⋅20=2405x=12⋅20=240, so x=2405=48x=5240​=48​ feet wide. Both 512125​ and 20484820​ reduce to 512125​, so the copy really is the same shape.
Problem
A design is 8 inches wide and 5 inches tall. The printed banner will be 20 inches wide. What height keeps the same shape without stretching?
Show a hint
  • Keep the same kind of measurement in the same spot. Put width over height for both pictures and set them equal, so 85=20x58​=x20​, where xx is the height you want.
  • Cross-multiply to clear the fractions. From 85=20x58​=x20​ you get 8x=5⋅208x=5⋅20, then divide both sides by 88 to find xx.
Show the full solution
Width over height on both sides. 85=20x58​=x20​ Cross-multiply to get 8x=5⋅20=1008x=5⋅20=100, so x=1008=25/2x=8100​=25/2​ inches, which is 12.512.5. Keeping the same shape just means keeping width over height fixed, which is what the proportion says.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A fruit punch keeps juice to water in the ratio 4:104:10. A bigger batch uses 6 cups of juice. Set up 410=6x104​=x6​ and solve. How many cups of water keep the same ratio?
Show the solution
Juice on top, water on the bottom in both fractions. 410=6x104​=x6​ Cross-multiply to get 4x=10⋅6=604x=10⋅6=60, so x=604=15x=460​=15​ cups of water. The cross-products agree, 4⋅15=604⋅15=60 and 10⋅6=6010⋅6=60.
Practice
A stage paint uses 3 oz pigment for every 7 oz base. A bigger batch uses 21 oz base. Set up 37=x2173​=21x​. How many ounces of teal pigment are needed?
Show the solution
Cross-multiply 37=x2173​=21x​ to get 7x=3⋅21=637x=3⋅21=63, so x=637=9x=763​=9​ ounces of teal pigment. Scaling checks it. The base tripled from 77 to 2121, so the pigment triples too, 3×3=93×3=9.
Practice
A pottery glaze uses 6 scoops of clay powder for every 5 cups of water. A big batch uses 40 cups of water. How many scoops of clay powder are needed?
Show the solution
Keep the ratio of scoops of clay powder to cups of water the same. Let xx be the scoops needed for 40 cups, so 65=x40.56​=40x​. Cross-multiply to clear the denominators, giving 5x=6×405x=6×40, so 5x=2405x=240. Divide both sides by 5 to get x=48x=48. The batch needs 4848​ scoops of clay powder.
Practice
A recipe uses 7 g of yeast for every 10 dinner rolls. The baker wants just 4 rolls. How many grams of yeast are needed?
Show the solution
Grams on top, rolls on the bottom in both fractions, so 710=x4107​=4x​. Cross-multiply to get 10x=7×4=2810x=7×4=28, then divide by 1010 and reduce, x=2810=14/5x=1028​=14/5​ grams, the same as 2.82.8.
Practice
A perfume sample uses 12 drops rose oil for every 21 drops sandalwood. A tester vial uses only 8 drops of rose oil. How many drops of sandalwood are in the tester?
Show the solution
Both mixes keep the same ratio of rose oil to sandalwood oil, so write a proportion with rose on top and sandalwood on the bottom in each fraction. 1221=8x2112​=x8​ Cross-multiply to clear the denominators. 12⋅x=21⋅812⋅x=21⋅8 12x=16812x=168 Divide both sides by 1212. x=16812=14x=12168​=14 The tester vial holds 1414​ drops of sandalwood oil.
Practice
Two flower beds keep the same ratio of 9 tulips to 12 daffodils. The second bed has 15 tulips. How many daffodils are in the second bed?
Show the solution
Put tulips on top and daffodils on the bottom in both fractions so the units match in matching positions. Let xx be the number of daffodils in the second bed. 912=15x129​=x15​ Cross-multiply to clear the denominators. 9⋅x=12⋅159⋅x=12⋅15 9x=1809x=180 Divide both sides by 99. x=1809=20x=9180​=20 The second bed has 2020​ daffodils.
Practice
A board game café trades 5 dollars for 65 tokens at a fixed rate. You hand over 8 dollars. How many tokens do you get?
Show the solution
Because the rate is fixed, the ratio of dollars to tokens is the same for both swaps. Keep dollars on top and tokens on the bottom in both ratios. 565=8x655​=x8​ Cross-multiply to clear the denominators. 5×x=65×85×x=65×8 5x=5205x=520 Divide both sides by 55. x=5205=104x=5520​=104 So 88 dollars gives you 104104​ tokens.
Practice
A pancake batter uses 5 cups flour for every 2 cups sugar. A big batch calls for 12 cups of sugar. How many cups of flour does it need?
Show the solution
The flour to sugar ratio stays the same, so set the recipe ratio equal to the big-batch ratio with flour on top and sugar on the bottom in both places. 52=x1225​=12x​ Cross-multiply to clear the denominators. 2x=5×122x=5×12 2x=602x=60 Divide both sides by 22. x=602=30x=260​=30 The giant batch needs 3030​ cups of flour.
Practice
A hiking map: 2 cm stands for 45 km. Two ranger stations sit 5 cm apart on the map. How many kilometers apart are they in real life?
Show the solution
Keep map centimeters on top and real kilometers on the bottom in both ratios, with xx standing for the real distance you are after. 245=5x452​=x5​ Cross-multiply to clear the denominators. 2⋅x=45⋅52⋅x=45⋅5 2x=2252x=225 Divide both sides by 22. x=2252=112.5x=2225​=112.5 So the two stations are 112.5112.5​ kilometers apart in real life.
Practice
A garden gnome (4 ft tall) casts a 5-foot shadow. A nearby water tower casts a 50-foot shadow at the same moment. How tall is the water tower in feet?
Show the solution
Both objects share the same height-to-shadow ratio, so put height on top and shadow on the bottom on each side. 45=h5054​=50h​ Cross-multiply to get 5h=4×50=2005h=4×50=200, so h=2005=40h=5200​=40​ feet tall.
Practice
A van holds a steady speed, covering 60 miles in 4 hours. At that same speed, how many miles does it cover in 7 hours?
Show the solution
The speed is steady, so miles over hours is the same both times. 604=x7460​=7x​ Cross-multiply to get 4x=60×7=4204x=60×7=420, so x=4204=105x=4420​=105​ miles.
Practice
A glassworker enlarges a 6-inch-wide by 9-inch-tall panel so the new width is 22 inches. Keeping the same shape, how tall is the enlarged panel in inches?
Show the solution
Width on top and height on the bottom for both panels. 69=22x96​=x22​ Cross-multiply to get 6x=9×22=1986x=9×22=198, so x=1986=33x=6198​=33​ inches tall. The check is that 22:3322:33 reduces to 2:32:3, the same shape as 6:96:9.
Practice
A sourdough starter uses 3 g starter for every 8 g flour. Tomorrow the baker uses 5 g flour. How many grams of starter should go in?
Show the solution
Starter on top, flour on the bottom in both ratios. 38=x583​=5x​ Cross-multiply to get 8x=3×5=158x=3×5=15, so x=15/8x=15/8​ grams of starter, which is 1.8751.875.
Practice
Two similar triangular sails. The small sail has a 12 cm bottom edge and 8 cm slanted edge. The enlarged sail has a 27 cm bottom edge. How long is its slanted edge in centimeters?
Show the solution
Because the sails are similar, the bottom edge and the slanted edge keep a constant ratio. Put bottom edges on top and slanted edges on the bottom in both ratios. 128=27x812​=x27​ Cross-multiply to clear the denominators. 12x=8×2712x=8×27 12x=21612x=216 Divide both sides by 1212. x=21612=18x=12216​=18 The slanted edge of the enlarged sail is 1818​ centimeters.
